summary: A fictional excerpt (Book 15, part 75) in which Ray questions Emma Whiston after the murder of a young child, Frederick's younger sibling-level household member, in a frontier setting. Emma says she tucked the boy into bed the night before after returning from the theatre, that he had been reading a picture book, and that Amah, their domestic who taught him to read, has told her only that he is dead and refused to give details. Ray tries to comfort her, avoids pressing too hard, and she guesses he is a soldier because he talks like a Marine.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, Ray questions grieving Emma Whiston about a child's murder, learns of the household's domestic Amah, and is pegged as a Marine.
key_facts: Emma Whiston says she tucked the murdered boy into bed the night before, after coming home from the theatre.
The boy had sneaked into the sitting room to read a picture book after the other children had fallen asleep.
Amah had made it a special task to teach the boy to read before the family reached New Holyoke.
Amah told Emma that the boy was dead but gave no details of how he died.
Emma says Amah sent her to her room like a little girl when she asked for more about the killing.
Emma says she has not really spoken with Frederick since the murder and has only spoken with Amah.
Amah has been with the Whiston family for years and raised Frederick and Emma from the moment Emma was born, after their mother first became ill.
Ray tells Emma that Becker will catch whoever did this.
Emma tells Ray he talks like a Marine, and she suspects he has been a soldier.
Emma mentions a Terran cousin, and Ray winks when she asks whether he has known many Marines.
